newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil - Prices seen sliding on rising output.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil - Prices seen sliding on rising output.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to soften this week on prospects of better harvests in the Philippines this month, Manila vegetable oil traders said on Monday.
"I expect prices to slide further from the previous week's $10 fall per tonne due to improving supply in key coconut growing areas in Mindanao island," said a senior trader.
Local prices of crude coconut oil are expected to remain steady at 19.40 pesos per kg and copra at 12.30 to 12.40 pesos per kg this week.
Traders said coconut supplies from Davao, General Santos and Zamboanga provinces, which account for around 39 percent of the Philippine output, have improved due to better weather conditions.
Philippine coconut products exports in the first three months of the year could reach 340,886 tonnes, according to preliminary data from trade group United Coconut Association of the Philippines Inc.
UCAP said the country exported a total of 552,239 tonnes of coconut products in the first quarter of 1996.

Preliminary data from the same trade group also showed the country's coconut oil exports from January to March dropped by 31.8 percent to 214,758 tonnes compared with 314,897 tonnes in the same period last year.

Traders said coconut oil exports for March alone could have been higher by 20,000 tonnes if not due to late ship arrivals. "Three ships carrying a total of 20,000 tonnes of coconut oil for the U.S. market for March deliveries arrived late so their cargoes will be included in April," said one trader.
